note: Sepolia receipts for ETHGlobal Tokyo 2026. Every field was fetched from the chain, not typed. CLAUDE.md: an unchecked receipt is worth less than no receipt, because it looks like evidence.

agentOwner.role: owns agentId 10518; its own write is refused

secondAddress.role: not owner, not an approved operator; its write is accepted
secondAddress.constraint: MUST NOT be approved on the agent token. isAuthorizedOrOwner is ERC-721's standard check, so one approve() would make this address refused too and the second shot would stop existing.

buyer.role: the client. A third account on purpose: reusing the second address from beat 1 would have made the demo's happy path the self-dealing case the project says it cannot prevent.

erc8004.provenance: erc-8004/erc-8004-contracts, deployed by the 8004 team, used unmodified
erc8004.andTheSpec: erc-8004.md:217 requires it. The ChaosChain reference implementation does NOT enforce it; we use the official contracts and show their check working first.

register.note: reckn-agent registers the agent. agentId 10518, minted to the EOA that is refused below.

selfWriteRefused.note: the agent's OWN address calls giveFeedback for its own agentId. Mined and reverted: Self-feedback not allowed. Sent with an explicit gas limit so estimation could not swallow it -- a refusal nobody can click is weaker than one they can.

secondAddressAccepted.note: a second address the same operator controls makes the identical call, and it succeeds. The check asks who you are; a second address answers it.

deployEscrow.note: RecknZkEscrow on Sepolia. No constructor, so the deployment carries no parameters. ENS Continuity asks the integration to target an existing project's testnet deployment; before tonight the escrow was on Arc only.

deployVerdictVerifier.note: RecknVerdictVerifier, pointing at SP1 v6.1.0 Groth16 0xb69f2584, which has NO owner. Not the SP1VerifierGateway: the gateway has an owner and its route for our selector is unfrozen, and a project whose claim is that no key decides should not put an owner in the adjudication path.

deployParentRegistry.note: our PermissionedRegistry, with ENS's own LabelStore 0x375c0820 (reached by ETHRegistrar -> ETH_REGISTRY -> LABEL_STORE, not guessed). Root roles held by the deployer FOR NOW; they are renounced after the adapter is granted.

deployResolverProxy.note: a UUPS proxy of ENS's PermissionedResolver implementation, created through ENS's own VerifiableFactory rather than a proxy of ours. The implementation is UUPS, so an EIP-1167 clone dies inside onlyProxy with 210 gas and no revert data.

approveRegistrar.note: MockUSDC allowance for the ETHRegistrar; ENSv2 registration fees are paid in MockUSDC on Sepolia.

commitName.note: commit-then-register: the commitment for reckn. MIN_COMMITMENT_AGE is 60 seconds, read from the registrar.

registerName.note: reckn registered on the REAL Sepolia ETHRegistrar for 0.613701 MockUSDC, with our PermissionedRegistry as its subregistry and our proxy as its resolver.

issueAgentSubname.note: agent.reckn.eth issued to the agent with roleBitmap 65536 = ROLE_RENEW ONLY. No ROLE_SET_RESOLVER: the agent owns its name and is not given the power to repoint its own record surface.

deployAdapter.note: SettlementRecord. No owner, no admin, no pause, no upgrade; open() and close() are callable by anyone and neither can choose an outcome.

grantAdapterOnResolver.note: the adapter is given the resolver role it needs to open and close windows.

revokeGhostGrant.note: an earlier grant went to 0xF3Ef66B7, the address the adapter was PREDICTED to land on before two funding transactions moved the nonce. Nothing is there and nothing can ever be: that CREATE address needs reckn-agent nonce 13, which was spent on a transfer. Revoked anyway -- 013 R-6 asks whether a second admin can appear later, and an unexplained root grant in the state is not an answer.

mintBuyerUsdc.note: MockUSDC for the buyer; its mint has no owner guard.

redeployAdapter.note: the FIXED adapter. The 09-25 one at 0x6691283d had two holes found overnight: close was a griefing weapon, and the name was a caller argument while the resolver scopes a role to the key alone. This one fixes the name at construction and puts it in the key.

grantNewAdapter.note: root on the resolver to the new adapter.

revokeOldAdapter.note: root taken away from 0x6691283d in the same run as the grant. Leaving it would have left a second admin on a surface whose whole claim is that nobody is in charge.

deployRehearsal.note: throwaway CREATE, pre-event, to prove the keystore/RPC/gas/explorer path before the window. WARNING: its address equals arc.json's RecknVerdictVerifier, because both are reckn-agent nonce 1 on their own chain. It is NOT a verifier.

fundSecondAddress.note: 0.005 ETH to the second address. Pre-event infrastructure.

stateReadBack.why: the owner wrote nothing and a second address wrote one record. This is state, not transactions, and it is what beat 1 claims.
routes to 0x740e02ce…, our resolver — E-Q3 satisfied on the real resolution path
stateReadBack.setResolver by the agent itself: STILL SUCCEEDS, because the deployer holds ROOT roles on the parent registry. S4's claim closes only after those are renounced, which happens after the adapter is granted. 013 section 1.1 discloses exactly this residue; it is not yet closed and is not claimed to be.

deployed.note: bytecode of the two Reckn contracts was compared against `forge inspect`, not against out/ (a stale artifact there produced a false mismatch once tonight). The verifier differs from its artifact only where its two immutables are substituted, and those hold the intended values.
deployed.SettlementRecord superseded: 0x6691283d8B77E1e22D08836c55E3f952c304Ccc1 -- the 09-25 adapter. Root revoked 09-26, so it can no longer open a window. Two defects, both found overnight and both recorded rather than quietly replaced: `close` was callable by anyone with no further condition, which let a stranger open a deal's one window and close it in the same block and make the record permanently unwritable; and the name was a caller argument, while the resolver derives a role's resource from the KEY alone, so a grant could be aimed at another name.

ens.family: the deployment family the spikes measured against; three live ENSv2 families exist on Sepolia and mixing them silently produces a name nobody can resolve
ens.name: reckn.eth

afterwards.THE AGENT writes: REFUSED, since 2026-09-26. It succeeded for the whole of this project's life, because the agent held root on the resolver and root overrides per-key roles. Both root roles were renounced (see the `renounce` section) and the three writes were re-read from chain immediately after: buyer refused, stranger refused, agent refused. 013 section 1.1 disclosed this residue in advance and this is it closing.

join.keyNamesTheName: the name is inside the key because the resolver cannot scope a role to a name -- measured 09-26: agent.reckn.eth and victim.reckn.eth with one key give one identical resource. Bytes written onto a foreign name therefore sit under a key that says whose record it is, and the canonical lookup for that name does not find them. The foreign write is not prevented; it is made unattributable.

joinFund.note: the buyer funds 250 USDC and names the verifier, pinned by codehash.

joinSettle.note: somebody who is NOT the buyer settles it on a real Groth16 proof. settleWithProof is permissionless.

joinOpen.note: the adapter opens the one window this deal will ever have, for the buyer fixed at funding. The caller chose nothing.

joinWrite.note: the BUYER writes the record. The agent never held this right.

joinClose.note: the window closes. The buyer's second write now reverts too.

supersededJoin0925.note: the 09-25 run, against adapter 0x6691283d. Superseded on 09-26, not deleted: it happened, the links to it are in this repository, and a record that drops what it now finds inconvenient is not a record. That adapter no longer holds root, so its window can never be opened again.

hookOnChain.what: 013 §4-9 on the real chain, 2026-09-26. Until this run the hook existed only on a fork, which would have made it the one part of this submission with no receipt.

fundHookDeal.note: the deal whose record opens the pool. Funded on the same escrow as every other deal here.

settleHookDeal.note: settled on the repository's committed Groth16 proof, by the agent -- settlement is permissionless.

openHookWindow.note: the window is opened and DELIBERATELY left unwritten, so the pool can be filmed refusing before it is filmed passing.

deployDemoToken0.note: demo scaffolding: the pool needs two tokens.

deployHook.note: CREATE2 through the deterministic factory 0x4e59b448, salt 20541, so that uint160(hook) & ALL_HOOK_MASK == BEFORE_SWAP_FLAG. Low 14 bits are 0x80.

deployPoolRouter.note: does the unlock dance so a swap is one transaction.

initializePool.note: on the REAL Sepolia PoolManager 0xE03A1074, fee 3000, tickSpacing 60, hooks = our hook.

addLiquidity.note: 100e18 of liquidity over [-600, 600]. beforeAddLiquidity is unflagged, so the hook is NOT consulted here -- the gate is on trading.

swapRefused.note: BEAT 5, shot one. A swap with no record. FAILED on chain, and refused by US: simulated at this same block, the ERC-7751 WrappedError carries target = the hook and reason = 0x43a7f347 NoSettledRecord(address). Sent with an explicit gas limit because a reverting call cannot be estimated.

recordWritten.note: the buyer writes, using the role the settlement granted. No root.

swapExecuted.note: BEAT 5, shot two. The SAME swap, now executed: 1.000000000000000000 token0 out.

recordCleared.note: the buyer clears the record while the window is still open.

swapRefusedAgain.note: BEAT 5, shot five. The same swap, refused again after the record was cleared. This is what stops the gate passing for an unrelated reason. Re-simulated at its own block like the first refusal: ERC-7751 WrappedError with target = the hook and reason = 0x43a7f347 NoSettledRecord(address). Both refusals were checked, not just the first.

windowClosed.note: the one window this deal will ever have.

eventProof.what: 013 §4-4. A proof that did not exist when the event started, verified on chain by the deployed verifier and settling a real deal.
eventProof.vkey: 0x00c2ee9999a00a5987a5b5c5261bee355bbb6e86c145429775d9fe89f496e16d  -- identical to the deployed RecknVerdictVerifier's immutable vkey
eventProof.terms: pre=42, post=142, floor=100 -- reexec's own defaults, NOT the shipped fixture's pre=2^64. Running `reexec --fixture` without --fixture-path would have replaced the committed fixture with a proof of different terms: every field still plausible, deal_binding and trace_hash quietly different. DEMO.md §5-5 warns about the overwrite; this is the sharper half.

eventFund.note: the buyer commits to the binding of a proof made 40 minutes earlier.

eventSettle.note: settled by a Groth16 proof GENERATED DURING THE EVENT -- 2026-09-26, 416.56 s wall on CPU, 15,972,262 constraints. Every other settlement in this record was decided by a proof committed to the tree before the event, which is disclosed and fine, but left one sentence unavailable: that the proving pipeline ran here. The agent was paid 250.000000 MockUSDC.

renounce.what: 013 §1.1's residue, closed. The account that is the agent deployed the registry and the resolver and held root on both; root overrides every per-key role the submission rests on. Renounced 2026-09-26. Irreversible: no role can be granted to a replacement adapter after this.
renounce.order: REGISTRY FIRST, then the resolver, and the order is the safety property. Interrupted between them, registry-first lands in a state that looks unfinished -- the agent can still write records, so every gate says so. Resolver-first lands in the state where take-check.sh printed 'Record.' while the agent could still repoint the name (found by review, on a fork).
renounce.readBack: resolver roleCount(ROOT) = 1 x ALL_ROLES -- exactly one holder left and it is the adapter. registry roleCount(ROOT) = 0 -- none at all. Then the three writes that decide beat 2: the buyer refused, a stranger refused, THE AGENT REFUSED. take-check.sh went green.

playgroundPool.what: A second pool, standing at the other end of the same argument. The evidence pool (0x68116b80) is SHUT and cannot reopen -- opened[dealId] never resets and the hook's key is fixed at construction, so clearing the record as beat 5's last act closed it permanently. This one was settled, written by the buyer, CLOSED, and only then did the renounce happen. It is open, and nobody can ever change it.

playgroundWrite.note: the buyer writes, under the role the settlement granted. NOT root.

playgroundClose.note: the buyer closes its own window. The right ends; the record stays.

playgroundPool.thenTheKeyWasDestroyed: see the renounce section -- it happened after this and before the trade below

strangerMint0.note: reckn-agent2 mints its own test tokens. The demo tokens are open to anyone.

strangerFund.note: and sends them to the router, which holds the pool's side and settles it.

strangerSwap.note: THE TRADE. Sent by an address that was never granted anything, is not the buyer, and never funded a deal -- after the only key that could have opened this pool was destroyed. 0.9871580343970613 token1 out.
